threshold_proximity_rule.statement: a discrete outcome (reason, status, boolean, settling sample index, None-ness) derived from a toleranced continuous quantity x by a threshold test x vs theta may differ between the implementations only where the Python value lies within x's registered tolerance of theta: |x_py - theta| <= tol(x_py) (combined with the threshold's own relative slack). Such a difference is recorded NOT_SCORED_AT_THRESHOLD with the quantity, theta and both values; any other difference fails. The dependent outcomes (status from reasons, objectives None-ness, the values that are masked or offered only on one side) of that vector are then not scored either and are listed

quantities.R_STAGE_DOMAIN: p_stage_max vs P_DOMAIN_PA (1 + 1e-12); compressor inlet pressure vs P_DOMAIN_PA
quantities.R_BISECTION: bisection_residual_rel vs BISECT_RTOL; a_eq vs the bracket ends (1 -/+ 1e-9)
quantities.R_SATURATED / saturated_end: u_cmd at the segment end vs 1 + 1e-9 and -1e-9 (tolerance: the u tolerance); orbit_quasi_static u_max vs 1
quantities.R_NOT_SETTLED / settling index: per sample |y - y_final| vs SETTLE_BAND |y_final| (tolerance: twice the trajectory tolerance of y, relative to |y_final|)

tolerance_classes.EXACT_VALUE: integers, strings, enums, booleans, statuses, reasons, ids, error classes, None / null, list lengths and orders, dict key SETS (Python dict insertion order carries no meaning in these records and is not compared), and floats that are copied (not computed): equal (floats by value, -0.0 == 0.0; non-finite floats are transported as the strings 'NaN', '+inf', '-inf' and compared as strings)
tolerance_classes.ULP_BOUNDED: |rust - py| <= k_ulp * ulp(py) OR |rust - py| <= r_rel * |py| OR |rust - py| <= a_abs, k_ulp / r_rel / a_abs fixed per observable group below (an absent clause is not applied); relative clause scaled by |py| (not max(1, |py|)): the observables span 1e-30 .. 1e9. ulp(py) = math.ulp(py)
tolerance_classes.SOLVER_TOLERANCE: convergence / solver status EXACT_VALUE; solution |rust - py| <= abs_tol + rel_tol * |py| with abs_tol / rel_tol fixed per entry below and tied to the solver's own tolerance; iteration and function-evaluation counts reported, not scored
tolerance_classes.EXACT_STREAM: not used (no RNG in either implementation)

registered.closed_form_and_steady: the Rust port repeats the reference operation order; scalar Python floats and glibc libm are reproduced exactly; the reference's numpy paths (area_for_pressure exp, steady_sweep, cascade_arrays, orbit sin) may differ by a few ulp (AVX512 SIMD loops); the cascade throughput Q = (A_c p2 - p3) / B_c can cancel and amplify that by up to ~1e6, so r_rel 1e-9 is the registered bound
registered.reservoir: Python floats only, identical algorithms: rounding-level
registered.transient: the integrators differ (scipy LSODA / BDF vs a Rust Radau IIA (5) with step doubling); a Python-only property of the reference measured before registration (no Rust involved; three chains of tests/test_design_f4_plenum.py type, LSODA rtol 1e-5 vs Radau rtol 1e-10): max relative error 1.7e-5 in p and 1.4e-5 in mdot, 1.3e-5 absolute in u, 1.4e-6 in xO, valve travel relative 1e-4, identical settling sample indices; BDF rtol 1e-8: 3.7e-8 / 4.0e-8 / 2.3e-8 / 1.2e-8. The registered tolerances are 100 x the integrator rtol (production 1e-3, reference 1e-5), i.e. ~60 x and ~250 x the measured reference error, covering the Rust integrator's own error at the same rtol

decision_rules.meaning_of_ADMITTED: A9.24 item 1: Rust becomes authoritative for the registered functions (within the registered domain); new production results for them come from Rust and carry implementation = rust, rust_commit and this contract id; the Python functions may then be retired from active execution. It is NOT physics validation.
decision_rules.no_retuning: tolerances, observables, inputs, n, seeds and rules are fixed; after NOT_ADMITTED only a code fix plus a new contract version with a fresh scoring_master_seed may follow; the failed report stays; no execution is discarded
decision_rules.disagreement_rule: never rewrite a Python result, golden, fixture or frozen dataset to make Rust pass (RM-R11)
decision_rules.observable_scope: observables are restricted to retained selected-architecture physics; an observable that depends on an excluded legacy path is not registered (RM-R20)
decision_rules.scoring_once: the scoring comparison runs once (scoring_master_seed); the harness refuses a second scoring run when parity_report_v1.json exists; development runs (development_master_seed) never write a report into the contract directory
decision_rules.per_test: every scored leaf of every vector meets its tolerance class (threshold-proximity differences recorded as NOT_SCORED_AT_THRESHOLD); every refusal has the same exception class in both implementations
decision_rules.verdict: ADMITTED iff every per-test, invariant (INV-P-01, -02, -04 compared; INV-P-03 and -05 by Rust tests), conservation, domain/error and schema check passes and every reference file matches sha256_at_registration; PARITY_PASS <=> ADMITTED, PARITY_FAIL <=> NOT_ADMITTED
decision_rules.proximity_limit: if more than 1 % of the scored discrete outcomes of an entry are NOT_SCORED_AT_THRESHOLD the entry fails (the rule is for isolated threshold coincidences, not for systematic drift)

what_this_is_not: not physics evidence or validation: parity shows the Rust code reproduces the Python reference, not that either is right

not a promotion of any provisional input (RM-R27): every PARAMETRIC_SENSITIVITY / PLACEHOLDER / TBD label of the reference is reproduced, never upgraded
not a gate PASS: absent determining evidence stays NOT_EVALUATED / INCOMPLETE_EVIDENCE / OUT_OF_DOMAIN / MODEL_ERROR (RM-R31)
